approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would reverse a federal environment minister's declaration that stopped a gold mine's tailings dam near Blayney, New South Wales.
It would repeal that declaration and prevent any future cultural heritage declarations under the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act from affecting the mine site.
The bill would take effect on the day it receives royal assent.
Repeals the environment minister's declaration made on 13 August 2024.
Prevents the minister from making any further declarations under the Heritage Protection Act that would affect the gold mine's construction or operation.
Defines the Blayney gold mine area to cover the full proposed mine site.
Regis Resources' proposed gold mine project near Blayney, New South Wales, and the Federal Environment Minister.

The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2024-11-20.11.2) to agree with the main idea of the bill, which means the bill will no longer be considered in parliament. In parliamentary jargon, the majority voted against reading the bill for a second time. The bill was sponsored by Tasmanian Senator [Jonathon Duniam](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/jonathon_duniam) (Liberal). ### What is the bill's main idea? According to the [bill homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/s1428), the bill: > *Repeals the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection (Kings Plains) Declaration 2024 and prevents the minister from making a declaration that would affect the construction or operation of a gold mine in the Blayney gold mine area.* Read more about Blayney gold mine decision on [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-08-19/mcphillamys-gold-project-mine-deemed-not-viable/104241418).
